source_trace.value: This is a strong independent open transport result, but it is not byte-equivalent to the closed original catalog and longer-window structure still requires sky-position/artifact controls.
This is a processed tile-time denominator, not yet exact non-overlapping geometric deg2-minute sky exposure.
Bruehl-Villarroel reported a positive nuclear-window association in their closed analysis sample and a large day-after comparison.
This result does not prove that every row in the closed 107,875-source catalog is artifactual and does not constitute byte-exact refutation of that unavailable sample.
The sign and significance of the reported positive +/-1 association do not transport into this independently selected, fully public POSS-I cohort.

This open result is qualitatively consistent with reanalyses that find observation/exposure normalization weakens the positive association, but non-equivalent catalogs and calendar definitions prevent treating them as one pooled replication.

Add plate/tile sky-position controls before interpreting longer-window negative structure. Observation date selects which right ascensions/fields were photographed; candidate density may vary with Galactic latitude, stellar density and catalog completeness.
Replace processed tile-minute proxy with exact non-overlapping valid WCS footprint area-time exposure.
Stratify by plate/copy/scanner/WCS quality and repaired-astrometry lineage where public metadata permit.
Add Kp/Ap, lunar and weather/visibility covariates from open sources with explicit missingness and provenance.
Freeze an event-time/lag design before reusing the exact-lag pattern as a confirmatory test.
Strict definition plus CRATER; UW excluded.

The public control reconstruction demonstrates that number of nuclear-test event rows and number of unique nuclear-test calendar dates are different quantities. Strict has 124 event rows but 121 unique dates; broad has 126 event rows but 123 unique dates. This may explain part of historical 124/125/126 ambiguity but does not prove byte/row equivalence to the unrecovered Bruehl-Villarroel calendar.
USA/USSR/UK AIRDROP/TOWER/SURFACE/ATMOSPH/BARGE/BALLOON/ROCKET/SHIP in the study window; CRATER and UW excluded.
The public cohort does not reproduce a positive day-after-test enhancement. Both frozen open calendars yield a modest negative point estimate whose confidence interval includes 1.

Significant negative point estimates several days BEFORE test dates are incompatible with a simple forward causal suppression story and instead flag temporal scheduling, observed-field composition or other confounding as mandatory targets.
Exact lag and blocked-permutation diagnostics were specified after inspection of the open primary +/-1 result and may not be treated as confirmatory discovery tests.

The primary +/-1 null remains strongly compatible with schedule-preserving permutations. The wider negative parametric signals are materially attenuated; only strict +/-4 crosses 0.05 in this simple post-hoc blocked diagnostic, while broad +/-4 does not. This is not sufficient evidence for nuclear suppression.

Negative Binomial NB2 with estimated dispersion, observation-date clustered covariance, log exposure_tile_min exposure, year_centered plus annual sine/cosine temporal covariates; Poisson retained as sensitivity.

Record the first fully public JANUS test of the reported POSS-I/nuclear-test association after removing dependence on the request-only 107,875-source VASCO catalog. The result tests transport of the association into an independently constructed, hash-pinned public cohort; it is not an exact replication of the closed sample.
JANUS POSS-I — Public-Only Nuclear-Association Reconstruction Result
